levelMapping: Ladder: AMTS (new grad) → MTS (≈SDE-2, ~2–5 YOE) → SMTS (senior, ~5–8 YOE) → LMTS (lead/staff, 8–12) → PMTS. SMTS sits around Google L4/L5 boundary; MTS ≈ Google L4 / Amazon SDE-2. For ~3.3 YOE expect an MTS offer (internally graded, e.g. 'MTS-3'); SMTS is reachable at 4–6 YOE with a strong loop, but hiring managers down-level — one 2026 HM said her SMTS engineers average ~7 YOE and moved a 5-YOE candidate to MTS, and a 6-YOE 'SMTS' interviewee was offered MTS-3. Level is negotiable with the recruiter after the loop.

process.summary: A recruiter/LinkedIn screen is followed by a proctored HackerRank OA (2 LC-medium problems, 60–90 min, ~80% cutoff), then a 3–5-round loop: 1–2 virtual DSA rounds (two problems each, full working code in a shared HackerRank IDE with all test cases passing), a 'design + code' LLD round (entities, SOLID, patterns, then runnable classes — often with a concurrency twist), an HLD round for SMTS and above (for MTS the HLD is usually folded into the hiring-manager round), and a hiring-manager round that is a genuine project-architecture deep-dive plus behavioral — frequently in person at the Bengaluru or Hyderabad office and sometimes containing a surprise coding (add polynomials) or design (login system) question. India hiring runs heavily through periodic MTS/SMTS/LMTS hiring drives with same-day eliminatory rounds. The bar in coding rounds is working, optimal code: several rejects cite one unsolved problem or missing 'design thinking' (assumptions/trade-offs not stated).

rounds.name: Recruiter screen
rounds.what: Background, current role, CTC and expectations, notice period; explains the format and sends the OA link (often 24 hours to 7 days to complete). Most loops start from LinkedIn/Instahyre outreach, referrals, or drive invites.
rounds.probes: Compensation band is often stated up front (recruiters quoted SMTS caps like ~33L base + 10% + $53K stock, or 70 LPA TC for senior). Follow-up is patchy — ghosting after OA/drives is widely reported, so keep nudging.

rounds.name: Online assessment (HackerRank)
rounds.what: 2 coding questions (occasionally 3), LC easy-medium to medium-hard, sometimes weighted 50+75 points. Proctored: camera and microphone on, full-screen enforced. Reported cutoff ~80% of test cases; partial scores count. A repeating bank: Minimum Ops to Reduce Integer to 0 (NAF), String Compression, max requests in a time window, longest subsequence-that-is-a-substring, 'almost sorted' min removals, spam-text classification, Delete and Earn variants.
rounds.probes: Since early 2026 some India reqs send a 'General Software Engineer Assessment (AI Interviewer)' HackerRank variant. One candidate was flagged for 'suspicious activity' for using pen and paper — keep hands visible and stay in frame.

rounds.name: Virtual DSA screen
rounds.what: Two problems in a shared HackerRank CodePair link: typically one easy-medium warm-up and one medium-hard. Problems are often story-wrapped (ride sharing, football scores, campaigns) so you must extract the pattern (sliding window, heap, BFS, DP). Expect to run code against the interviewer's test cases.
rounds.probes: Brute force → optimal progression, exact time/space complexity (one SMTS interviewer probed how String.split and StringBuilder.append work internally), edge cases. Variants of your own OA questions are sometimes re-asked.

rounds.name: Onsite DSA round(s)
rounds.what: Same format, harder: LC medium/hard. Grids/graphs (islands, rotting oranges, course schedule, Dijkstra/knight moves), DP (knapsack, LIS, maximal square/rectangle, job scheduling), heaps/streams (median, top-K, halve-K-times), stacks (remove-K duplicates, asteroid collision, max stack), design-a-data-structure (LRU/LFU, getRandom O(1), All O'one).
rounds.probes: Some interviewers refuse to let you code until the optimal approach is agreed; others demand all test cases green. A 2026 reject: solved both mediums fully and still didn't advance — the bar can be 'no nitpicks'.

rounds.name: LLD / design + code
rounds.what: 'Design + code': clarify requirements, model entities/classes with SOLID and patterns, then write clean (often runnable) code — Splitwise, elevator, BookMyShow, parking lot, Ludo, meeting scheduler, message queue, connection pool. Frequently has a concurrency/thread-safety component (blocking queues, synchronized pools, scheduler).
rounds.probes: Extensibility (new expense/split types), design-pattern vocabulary (observer, strategy, state), DB schema for the entities, thread safety. At MTS level this round is sometimes swapped for a second DSA round without warning — prepare both. One Hyderabad reject traced to doing LLD in Python when the interviewer wanted static-typed (Java) modelling.

rounds.name: HLD / system design (SMTS+)
rounds.what: Real-world, deliberately ambiguous systems rather than textbook prompts: notification service with client data ingestion and filtering, marketing campaign system, flash sale, payment platform, metric collection, property marketplace migration. MTS loops usually skip a dedicated HLD round; it appears inside the HM round instead.
rounds.probes: Interviewers chase deep dives, not complete diagrams: distributed transactions/saga, contention and double-booking, idempotency, failure handling and self-healing, DB choice and sharding trade-offs, CDC, cache migration, back-of-envelope numbers. An SMTS reject letter explicitly cited not 'demonstrating the level of design thinking expected' — state assumptions and trade-offs aloud.

rounds.name: Hiring manager round
rounds.what: Deep dive into your current project's architecture (often drawn on a whiteboard), ownership, trade-offs, what you'd redo; behavioral: why Salesforce, why switching, conflicts, mentoring, on-call, AI tool usage. Panels sometimes pair the HM with a senior IC or Director who drives the technical grilling.
rounds.probes: Surprise technical asks are common: add two polynomials (reported twice), design a login system, an HLD case study, event-driven/Kafka internals (poison messages, DLQ, race conditions), SDLC/testing/rollback strategies. HM 'No Hire' overturns two prior Hires, so don't coast — bring a resume you can defend line by line.

rounds.name: Extra fitment / second HM round
rounds.what: When the original req closes or feedback is mixed, recruiters add a team-fitment round with the team's lead or a new team's HM (project discussion, no coding). Pool/drive candidates are routinely re-matched to other teams after positive loops.
rounds.probes: Treated as a culture/level check; consistency with earlier answers matters.

process.indiaNotes: India (Hyderabad + Bengaluru) is the main MTS/SMTS/LMTS hiring ground and runs on recurring hiring drives (roughly monthly through 2025–26: virtual DSA screen a day or two before, then same-day onsite eliminatory rounds — DSA → LLD/HLD → HM — with candidates sent home between rounds). HM rounds are usually in person even when everything else is virtual; Salesforce sends Uber vouchers (~₹2k) and provides meals. Expect slow post-loop phases: offer approval by a 'business team' takes 1–4+ weeks, roles get closed/paused after positive loops with redirection to other teams, and recruiter ghosting is the single most-reported complaint. US loops differ: HM call often comes first, then OA, two tech screens and an onsite with more HLD weight (TinyURL, parking lot) and CodeSignal appears occasionally. Frontend SMTS loops replace LLD with JS/React fundamentals and frontend system design (Google Maps, WhatsApp Web).
process.timeline: OA within a week of the screen; interviews 1–4 weeks after OA (drives compress all rounds into 1–2 days); verdicts in 2–7 days; offer letter 1–4 weeks after verdict due to business-approval steps. End to end: ~3–8 weeks when smooth, but multi-month stalls (role closures, hiring pauses, re-matching) are common.
tips: Working code wins rounds: interviewers expect all HackerRank test cases green; practice typing out full solutions fast, not just approaches.
Narrate and get buy-in before every block of code — the strongest accepted loops all describe thinking out loud and agreeing the approach first (drawing on Excalidraw/whiteboard helps).
State assumptions and trade-offs explicitly in design rounds; 'good code, weak design thinking' is a documented SMTS rejection reason.
Drill the OA bank (LC 2571, 443, 740, sliding-window request counting, subsequence-vs-substring DP, almost-sorted LIS) — questions repeat across months and levels.
Prepare LLD in Java-style static typing with SOLID vocabulary, and expect to also handle concurrency (blocking queues, locks) inside the LLD round.
Don't trust the advertised round plan: LLD rounds turn into DSA, HM rounds spring HLD or coding questions, and MTS candidates do get LLD (Ludo, 2026-09).
Own your resume end-to-end: HM rounds grill current-project architecture, Kafka/event-driven internals, rollback and testing strategy; a stale resume sank an otherwise 2-Hire loop.
Build interview stamina — drives run 3 rounds back-to-back in a day, and fatigue in the final HM round is a reported cause of rejection.
Discuss level early: SMTS vs MTS is fluid around 4–6 YOE and can be negotiated with the recruiter after feedback.
Be patient but proactive post-loop: positive feedback often sits waiting on business approval; keep following up and ask about other teams if the req closes.
process.notes: OA platform is HackerRank for India (75 min typical; one LMTS report used HackerEarth, one US report CodeSignal); a proctored 'AI Interviewer' HackerRank variant appeared for India reqs in 2026. No separate 'Ohana/values' round in recent India MTS/SMTS loops — culture-fit questions live inside the HM round (US/frontend loops sometimes add a dedicated culture round). Language is free (Java dominates reports; one role required C++; Python accepted but risky for LLD). Live rounds are language-agnostic LeetCode-style, not practical/bug-squash style. LLD exists as a dedicated round for both MTS and SMTS (with code expected); HLD as a standalone round is mostly SMTS/LMTS. Compensation anchors from 2026 reports: MTS ~28–30L base + ~$52K RSU/4yr + ~10% bonus (TC ~43–50 LPA); SMTS up to ~70 LPA TC quoted in a drive.

dsa.title: Minimum Operations to Reduce an Integer to 0
dsa.variant: OA version raises the constraint to n < 2^60, so use long and the NAF (non-adjacent form) greedy on the two low bits rather than DP.
dsa.evidence: Salesforce's most-repeated OA question: SMTS OA 2026-05 and 2026-07, LMTS OA 2025-07, SMTS Bangalore OA 2025-05.

dsa.title: Maximum requests in a time window
dsa.statement: Given an array of request timestamps and an integer windowSize, return the maximum number of requests that fall inside any continuous window of that length (timestamps in [t, t+windowSize) count). Sort if needed, then slide two pointers maintaining the window. Re-asked verbally in a 2026 virtual screen alongside Merge Intervals.
dsa.evidence: OA staple: SDE-2 OA 2026-02, SMTS OA 2026-05, MTS drive OA 2026-08 (then revisited in the screen).

dsa.title: Longest subsequence of x that is a substring of y
dsa.statement: Given strings x and y (each up to ~2000 chars), return the length of the longest subsequence of x that appears as a contiguous substring of y. LCS-style DP where the y-dimension must stay contiguous: dp[i][j] = longest subsequence of x[..i] ending exactly at y[j]. One OA paired it with also returning the plain LCS length.
dsa.variant: Also asked live in a Feb 2026 MTS round ('subsequence + substring').
dsa.evidence: OA: MTS 2025-06, SDE-2 2026-02, SMTS rejected OA 2025-10; live round 2026-02.

dsa.title: String Compression
dsa.variant: OA variants: keep single chars uncounted (ab2c3d), or count every run including singles (abaasass → a1b1a2s1a1s2).
dsa.evidence: Recurring OA question: SMTS OA 2025-03, 2025-06, 2025-07, rejected OA 2025-10; #2 in the LC company tag.

dsa.title: Minimum removals to make an array 'almost sorted'
dsa.statement: An array is 'almost sorted' if deleting at most one element makes it strictly ascending. Given n unique integers, return the minimum number of elements to remove so the remainder is almost sorted. Reduces to a longest-increasing-subsequence computation that tolerates one 'gap'; an O(n log n) solution is expected and brute force TLEs.
dsa.evidence: OA: SMTS March 2025, SMTS June 2025 (most failed hidden cases), full-stack loop 2025-06.

dsa.title: Spam text classification
dsa.statement: Given up to 10^3 texts and up to 10^5 spam words (combined length ≤10^7), label each text 'spam' if it contains at least two spam-word occurrences (every occurrence counts). One version is case-sensitive, another case-insensitive. Tokenize each text and count hash-set hits; constraints force attention to total input size.
dsa.evidence: OA: SMTS Aug 2025 loop (offer track), repeat report Sep 2025, MTS OA Jun 2025 (case-insensitive).

dsa.title: Delete and Earn
dsa.variant: OA reskin: 'maximum power you can collect from a list if choosing power[i] bans power[i]±1' — same house-robber-on-values DP.
dsa.evidence: OA: Jul 2025 (modified), Sep 2025 (direct), 'powers' variant Jul 2025.

dsa.title: Partition campaigns into weeks minimizing sum of weekly maxima
dsa.statement: Given campaign costs in fixed order and k weeks, split the array into k non-empty contiguous groups (at least one campaign per week); each week's cost is the maximum in its group, and you minimize the total of weekly maxima. Interval DP with precomputed range maxima — structurally LC 1335 (Minimum Difficulty of a Job Schedule) with max instead of sum-of-max nuance; naive O(n^2 k) can TLE at OA constraints.
dsa.evidence: Onsite round Jun 2026, MTS virtual round 2 in a Sep 2025 offer loop, LMTS OA Mar 2025 (13/15 cases, rest TLE).

dsa.title: Merge Intervals
dsa.variant: Asked as variants: the 2026-01 onsite gave a merge-intervals mutation where ruling out wrong approaches aloud mattered.
dsa.evidence: Virtual screen of Aug 2026 MTS drive; tech screen of Jan 2026 MTS offer loop; onsite variant in another Jan 2026 loop; heavy LC-tag presence.

dsa.title: LRU Cache
dsa.variant: Often paired with LFU in the same round ('design both from scratch'), with follow-ups on complexity and further optimization; also appears in DSA+LLD hybrid rounds with an expected specific approach.
dsa.evidence: Virtual round May 2026 (LRU+LFU both coded), round 4 of Sep 2026 MTS loop, Feb 2026 Hyderabad round 2, offered as a choice in a Feb 2026 round.

dsa.title: LFU Cache
dsa.variant: Sometimes framed as the whole 'LLD' round (~100 lines expected, approach mattered more than compiling).
dsa.evidence: LLD round of a Dec 2025 SMTS loop; paired with LRU in May 2026 and Feb 2026 rounds; strong LC-tag signal.

dsa.title: Number of Islands
dsa.variant: Usually a variant (counting/area twist); in one LMTS screen it was Q1 of two with a working solution required.
dsa.evidence: Tech screen Apr 2026 (variant), onsite May 2026, LMTS screen Nov 2025, MTS3 loop Dec 2025, DSA round 2024-04.

dsa.title: Find Median from Data Stream
dsa.variant: Asked alongside Number of Islands in the same onsite; two-heap solution expected.
dsa.evidence: Onsite round 3 of a selected May 2026 MTS loop; in the LC company tag.

dsa.title: Course Schedule II
dsa.variant: Minor variants; topological-sort framing sometimes hidden in a story.
dsa.evidence: Onsite round 5 of Apr 2026 MTS offer loop ('minor variant, solved completely'); round 1 of Jun 2026 MTS loop.

dsa.title: Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling
dsa.variant: Interviewer steered away from greedy toward recursion → memo → bottom-up DP + binary search for the next compatible job (O(n log n)).
dsa.evidence: Round 1 of the Aug 2026 India MTS drive (verdict Hire).

dsa.title: Coin Change II
dsa.variant: Coin-change family recurs: classic Coin Change (LC 322) in a Jan 2025 SMTS round and a Dec 2025 OA; a 'coin change variation' in a Nov 2024 Hyderabad drive.
dsa.evidence: Onsite DSA round of Jun 2026 Bangalore MTS offer loop; LC 322 reports 2025-01 and 2025-12.

dsa.title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
dsa.variant: Asked as 'design a data structure with O(1) insert/delete/getRandom, uniform probability'; a similar 'Set with get/put/iterate/clear in O(1)' appears at peer companies.
dsa.evidence: Onsite DSA round of Jun 2026 Bangalore MTS offer loop.

dsa.title: Ways to Split Array Into Three Subarrays
dsa.variant: Salesforce version ('Good Ways to Split'): count splits into A1,A2,A3 where S2 ≤ S1 + S3, answer mod 1e9+7 — prefix sums + two binary searches; partial implementation with a solid approach was accepted.
dsa.evidence: Virtual screening of Jun 2026 Bangalore MTS offer loop.

dsa.title: ATM queue simulation
dsa.statement: n people queue at an ATM, each wanting to withdraw amount[i], but a single transaction dispenses at most K. Anyone still owed money rejoins the back of the queue. Return the order in which people leave. Simulate with a queue, or compute each person's finish round ceil(amount/K) and stable-sort by it.
dsa.evidence: Virtual screening of Jun 2026 Bangalore MTS offer loop (all tests passed).

dsa.title: Halve elements K times to minimize array sum
dsa.statement: Given an array and k operations where each operation picks any element, halves it, and puts it back, return the minimum possible total sum after k operations. Max-heap greedy: always halve the current maximum. (Mirror of LC 2530, which maximizes with ceil.)
dsa.variant: Asked as a rapid-fire third question in a Nov 2025 round and as problem B in a Jun 2026 onsite (solved with a max heap in ~10 min).
dsa.evidence: MTS round Nov 2025; Bangalore MTS onsite Jun 2026.

dsa.title: Top K Frequent Words
dsa.variant: Streaming variant (Aug 2026): support add(number) and query top-K most frequent over an infinite stream, efficiently interleaved. Older variant: top-K strings with lexicographic tie-break.
dsa.evidence: Tech screen of Apr 2026 MTS offer loop; streaming version in Aug 2026 round 1; 2024-04 round.

dsa.title: Maximal Square
dsa.evidence: Asked in two separate Jul 2026 MTS loops (one paired with Maximal Rectangle, one with LIS).

dsa.title: Maximal Rectangle
dsa.variant: Follow-up to Maximal Square in the same round; a clean dry-run of the histogram approach was accepted when time ran out.
dsa.evidence: Round 1 of Jul 2026 MTS loop (2.5 YOE, verdict Hire).

dsa.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
dsa.variant: Both brute force and the optimal patience/binary-search solutions expected.
dsa.evidence: DSA round of Jul 2026 MTS loop (both solved, still rejected — bar is high).

dsa.title: Rotting Oranges
dsa.evidence: DSA round 1 of Dec 2025 MTS offer loop; also in a Dec 2025 MTS3 loop round 1.

dsa.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
dsa.evidence: DSA round 1 of Dec 2025 MTS offer loop (paired with Rotting Oranges).

dsa.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
dsa.variant: Space-complexity nitpick: O(1) given the bounded alphabet, not O(n).
dsa.evidence: SMTS Aug 2025 round 1, SMTS Feb 2025 screen, MTS round late 2025 (Hyderabad loop).

dsa.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
dsa.variant: Nasty 2025 variant: input arrives as parent[] and values[] lists, so you must build the tree yourself before solving. 2023 follow-up: also return the path.
dsa.evidence: SMTS round Oct 2025 (parent-array input), SMTS coding round Jan 2025, Gurgaon drive round 2 Nov 2023.

dsa.title: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates in String II
dsa.variant: Also phrased as 'repeatedly remove k consecutive identical characters until stable'.
dsa.evidence: Onsite DSA round 1 of Feb 2026 MTS offer (43 LPA) loop, SMTS round Oct 2025, 'Remove K Duplicates' Feb 2026 round.

dsa.title: First Missing Positive
dsa.evidence: Onsite DSA round 1 of Feb 2026 MTS offer loop (paired with LC 1209; both solved).

dsa.title: Minimum Knight Moves (knight traversal on chessboard)
dsa.variant: Framed as 'minimum time for a knight from start to end position' — plain BFS.
dsa.evidence: Round 2 (Strong Hire) of Jul 2026 MTS loop.

dsa.title: Reorder a bounded-displacement stream (UDP packet ordering)
dsa.statement: Numbers arrive as a stream where each value is at most n positions away from its sorted position (buffer size n). Emit them in sorted order without storing the whole stream: keep a min-heap of size n+1, popping the minimum as each new element arrives.
dsa.evidence: Round 2 of Jul 2026 MTS loop (Strong Hire); similar 'stream of events printed by end time' in Round 2 of a Mar 2025 MTS loop.

dsa.title: Task scheduling under memory and type-concurrency constraints
dsa.statement: Given task types, per-task memory, and a server memory limit M, at most 2 tasks of the same type may run simultaneously and the running tasks' memory must stay ≤ M; each round takes 1 time unit. Find the minimum time to run all tasks (e.g. types [A,A,A,B,B,C], memory [2,2,3,4,1,2], M=5 → 3). Greedy packing per round with the pairing constraint.
dsa.evidence: DSA round of Apr 2026 MTS loop.

dsa.title: Grid shortest path with jumps of 1..K
dsa.statement: In an m×n grid with obstacles you move in 4 directions, but each move may jump 1 to K cells in that direction. Given source and destination, return the minimum number of moves. BFS where each node expands up to 4K neighbors, stopping a ray at obstacles (cousin of LC 1345/Zuma-style jump BFS).
dsa.evidence: DSA round of Apr 2026 MTS loop (paired with the task-scheduling problem).

dsa.title: Count ways to split a digit string into primes
dsa.statement: Given an integer as a string (digits in fixed order, whole string used), count the ways to partition it into substrings that are each prime (e.g. '11375' → 3: [11,37,5], [11,3,7,5], [113,7,5]). DP over positions with primality checks on bounded-length chunks.
dsa.evidence: DSA round 1 of Jun 2026 MTS selected loop (paired with Course Schedule II).

dsa.title: Max Stack (O(1) ops), follow-up Maximum Frequency Stack
dsa.variant: LMTS round: interviewer refused to let code start until the design reached O(1) per operation, then demanded a fully working implementation with tests; last 15 min were Maximum Frequency Stack (LC 895) approach-only. Related: 'queue with getMax in O(1)' (monotonic deque) in a Nov 2025 SMTS round.
dsa.evidence: LMTS Sep 2025 offer loop round 1; queue-with-max SMTS Nov 2025.

dsa.title: Asteroid Collision
dsa.variant: Aug 2026 reskin: 'balls' with direction ±1 and strength; return surviving indexes after all collisions — same monotonic-stack simulation hidden in a story.
dsa.evidence: SMTS DSA round Sep 2025 (offer); ball-collision version in Aug 2026 SMTS drive round 1.

dsa.title: Furthest Building You Can Reach
dsa.variant: Asked as 'peaks with climbing-kit resources and a limited helicopter' — identical heap-greedy under a resource-allocation story.
dsa.evidence: DSA round of Aug 2026 SMTS in-person drive.

dsa.title: Minimum Window Substring
dsa.variant: Word-level version in Aug 2026 SMTS screen: given a string of n words and k required words, return the minimum contiguous word window containing all of them (empty string if any missing). Also asked inside a 2025 HM round.
dsa.evidence: MTS Round 1 Apr 2025 (solved O(n)); HM round of Apr 2025 Oracle/Salesforce/Okta writeup; word-window screen Aug 2026.

dsa.title: Word Break
dsa.evidence: MTS round 1 Oct 2025 (candidate only reached recursion with hints).

dsa.title: Time Based Key-Value Store
dsa.variant: Interviewer drilled specifically on the binary-search reasoning.
dsa.evidence: DSA round of the restarted MTS process (offer, posted Jan 2026).

dsa.title: Remove Duplicates From an Unsorted Linked List
dsa.variant: OA variant: keep exactly one occurrence of each value (plain dedupe) in one report; remove all values that ever repeat in the other.
dsa.evidence: SMTS OA Nov 2025 (paired with a Kth-largest variant), SMTS OA in the Mar 2026 rejected loop.

dsa.title: Count complementary string pairs (palindromic concatenation)
dsa.statement: Two strings are complementary if some permutation of their concatenation is a palindrome. Given an array of strings, count unordered pairs (i,j) that are complementary (e.g. 'abac'+'cab' → 'abaccab' rearranges to 'bcaacb'... palindrome). Encode each string as a 26-bit parity mask; pairs match when XOR of masks has ≤1 bit set — count with a mask-frequency map.
dsa.evidence: OA of the Mar 2026 SMTS loop.

dsa.title: Reorganize String
dsa.variant: Related OA: minimum substitutions so no two adjacent characters are equal (count runs). Older round: can characters be rearranged into a palindrome.
dsa.evidence: DSA round of Mar 2026 SMTS loop (with Combination Sum II); adjacent-chars OA Jul 2025 and in a full-stack loop 2025-06; palindrome-rearrange 2023-09.

dsa.title: Combination Sum II
dsa.variant: Backtracking is a persistent theme: Subsets II with a sorted-output constraint (Apr 2025), Generate Parentheses (May 2026), Permutations (Aug 2026), generic 'backtracking problem' in Feb 2026.
dsa.evidence: DSA round of Mar 2026 SMTS loop; Subsets II variant Apr 2025; backtracking Q in Feb 2026 SMTS round 1.

dsa.title: Generate Parentheses
dsa.evidence: Round 1 of May 2026 SMTS offer loop (paired with Design BookMyShow); top of the LC company tag's 3-month window.

dsa.title: Add two polynomials
dsa.statement: Represent two polynomials (coefficient, exponent pairs — as lists or linked lists) and return their sum, merging like exponents and dropping zero coefficients. Deceptively simple HM-round warm-up asked verbally with no examples: the test is whether you clarify representation and requirements before coding.
dsa.evidence: Asked in two separate HM rounds: Dec 2025 SMTS loop and Mar 2026 Hyderabad MissionForce SMTS loop.

dsa.title: Convert Sorted List to Binary Search Tree (in place)
dsa.variant: Aug 2026 version: convert a sorted doubly linked list into a height-balanced BST without allocating new nodes (rewire in place). Mar 2025 loop asked the classic version on a whiteboard in the HM round.
dsa.evidence: Round 1 of Aug 2026 MTS selected loop; onsite techno-managerial round Apr 2025.

dsa.title: Path With Maximum Probability
dsa.variant: Graph rounds also featured Dijkstra-flavored problems ('shortest path marking + count decreasing-distance paths', a double-Dijkstra onsite problem Aug 2026) and diameter of an acyclic undirected graph (Jul 2026).
dsa.evidence: Round 3 of Sep 2026 MTS loop; double-Dijkstra onsite Aug 2026; Dijkstra-based round Nov 2025.

dsa.title: House Robber
dsa.variant: House Robber II (LC 213) was the second (deciding) question in a Nov 2025 LMTS screen — a partial DP solution there caused the rejection.
dsa.evidence: Round 3 of Sep 2026 MTS loop; LC 213 in Nov 2025 LMTS online round.

dsa.title: Knapsack / budget-selection DP family
dsa.statement: Recurring knapsack dressings: pick projects under a budget to maximize value (pick/not-pick DP, Sep 2026); unbounded knapsack with full working code and complexity discussion (Feb 2026); a 'knapsack variant' LC medium/hard in an Aug 2025 SMTS round; a 0-1 knapsack look-alike in an Oct 2025 OA. Be fluent in 0/1, unbounded, and bottom-up conversions.
dsa.evidence: Four loops 2025-08 through 2026-09.

dsa.title: Meeting Rooms II / max meetings in a room
dsa.variant: Asked as 'how many meetings can be conducted in a room' (N-meetings greedy) and as a Meeting-Rooms-II look-alike; a Nov 2025 Hyderabad candidate was rejected for missing the optimal approach.
dsa.evidence: Glassdoor MTS Hyderabad Nov 2025; Aug 2026 MTS round 1 (greedy, N-meetings style); Glassdoor MTS Bengaluru Feb 2025 round 2.

design.title: Design a notification service
design.prompt: Recurs in several shapes: classic multi-channel notification service (priority levels, templates, user preferences, DND); a 2026 version framed as a Klaviyo-like platform ingesting event streams from clients (Amazon/Zomato-type) with filtering and processing before fan-out.
